title: Silicon & Sepia - The Vintage Desk Writing Environment

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A writer's desk: flick the lamp on to light the work, papers lie scattered and rotated, photographs overlap with curl, a cup of tea drains as you work.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: A 3D-transformed desk scene is the article index: polaroids and scattered papers are clickable; picking up a paper opens the full written piece in a reader with drop caps. Hover hit-testing uses real pointer geometry (elementsFromPoint) so whichever pixel is under the cursor lifts, matching true overlapping-photo behavior. The lamp is a literal light/dark toggle; the tea cup is a session timer.

design_tokens.borders: Photo white frames and paper edges; slight rotations (2-8 degrees) on every prop
design_tokens.elevation: 3D-transformed layered props with soft cast shadows; lifted items translate toward the viewer
design_tokens.typography: Drop-cap serif reader for article content; handwritten/typewriter accents on props

interactive_mechanics: Lamp toggle switches ambient light (light/dark mode as a physical switch)
Pick up a scattered paper to open the corresponding article reader
Polaroids lift under the true cursor pixel, not a bounding box
Tea cup drains as a playful session/progress indicator
usability_notes: Strong for personal writing portfolios where editorial warmth is the brand. Navigation via scattered props is inherently low-scanability - pair with a conventional index or strong category labels. Wide 3D scenes compress poorly on mobile; needs a list-mode fallback. Source: Devpost project documentation (self-reported mechanics).
